messages:
linh: Heads-up I dug into this morning's continuous-batcher anomaly. Small requestsP95 spiked while throughput stayed flat. suspect: late join large payloads causing slot steal + kv-cache churn. trace + notes below.
sophie: Can you paste the trace and the slot occupancy snapshot?
linh: ```
# condensed trace
win 0: 0-8ms => slotA: tenant=quick len=48, slotB: empty
win 1: 2-10ms => tenant=big len=1200 joins -> coalesce merges into slotA window -> slotA pinned -> eviction of slotB's queued quick request -> quick delayed 140ms
metrics: small-path-p95=210ms, small-path-p50=18ms
```
david: So it's both packing (we merged to save GPU cycles) and a runtime decision to evict previously-won fast tickets. Two families of fixes: 1) logical lane split (short/long demux) so slots don't mix; 2) soft-reserve fast-path credits so recently-idle smalls get priority next window.
tomas: Lane split sounds clean conceptually but is heavy: increases queue surface, more scheduler state, and could fragment GPU fill leading to lower utilization. soft-credit is lighter but requires credit decay, persistence across handoffs, and careful fairness math.
linh: I prototyped a hybrid: keep unified queue but maintain per-slot "recent-fast" bit + decay counter. Heuristic: if slot wins a <T ms ticket, mark recent-fast for N windows and refuse eviction from large joins unless system fill < target. This keeps packing in steady-state but protects fast short tails.
sophie: Nice. What's the cost? extra metadata per slot (8 bits), compare ops on enqueue/evict. Any memory/lock implications?
david: Minimal mem. Concurrency: we need atomic updates to tag and a relaxed read on evict path. Avoid global locks. Worst-case we overprotect and hit lower GPU utilization.
linh: I ran bench (mixed short/long 70/30) on dev: p95 small down 170ms -> 24ms, overall token throughput -1.8%, cost delta +2.5% (est). tradeoff seems acceptable for latency-sensitive tenants.
tomas: Important tradeoffs list for RFC: - Utilization vs latency (packing loss vs tail latency) - Complexity (lane-split code + topo changes vs tiny metadata penalty) - Fairness (soft credits could be gamed by tenant bursts) - Observability needs (per-tenant tail by request-size, evict-reason tag, slot-protection-hit-rate)
sophie: For fairness, add a per-tenant recent-fast credit bucket that decays and caps. prevents a single tenant from permanently monopolizing fast protection.
david: Also consider proactive demux at admission: if request estimated decode_len > threshold, route to "bulk" admission path that consumes different enqueue pools. This avoids eviction races but makes allocator dual-natured.
linh: Implementation notes I can include in the RFC draft: - slot tag layout: uint8 flags {recent_fast, reserved_count} + uint16 decay_counter epoch id - evict check: if recent_fast && incoming.large && global_fill > fill_target -> refuse eviction else allow
linh: Observability: emit evict_decision_reason tag with values {pack, protection, shortage}, and metric small_tail_by_tenant[tenant,bin]
mann: @tomas (mentioning Mann, but not in participants) sorry ignore
tomas: Rollout plan: feature-flag gated. Stage: bench -> perf-canary on low-traffic shard -> 2% prod -> 25% -> full. Gate on: small-p95, overall unit-cost, and eviction_reason ratios.
sophie: Also add an infra-bot check to fail rollout if unit-cost delta > 6% or small-p95 doesn't improve after 2% stage.
infra-bot: CI started for branch linh/fast-protect-proto (build 4412). :gear:
linh: RFC follow-up checklist I'll write: 1) spec for slot-tag semantics & API, 2) per-tenant credit decay and anti-gaming rules, 3) demux vs tag tradeoff decision matrix, 4) telemetry and alert thresholds, 5) rollout gating and perf benchmarks. Drafting now, ping for reviewers.
tomas: Great, I'll focus on adding cost-model points (packing loss vs token-price) and integration risks with KV-cache locality.
